text:
maya: Heads-up — we got reports of gRPC streaming sessions being disconnected when routed through the edge NGinx farm in eu-west-1 this morning. Seen from prod and staging.
jon: saw a spike in stream resets around 07:12-07:18 UTC, same namespace. Any logs?
maya: attaching snippets, logs show a lot of RST_STREAM/CANCELs and periodic TCP FINs from the ALB side. Example: 
```
[2026-03-18T07:14:03Z] stream_id=421 error=RST_STREAM code=CANCEL peer=10.0.12.45:41812
[2026-03-18T07:14:03Z] tcp: FIN from 10.0.0.5:443 -> 10.0.12.45:51812
```
carlos: could be idle timeout somewhere. ALB default idle timeout is 60s; nginx upstream keepalive/timeouts maybe shorter. Are streams long-lived?
maya: yes, chat streams can be idle for 30-90s between user tokens. We normally use HTTP/2 with periodic application-level pings. We also have connection-level keepalive configured, but maybe something in the edge is dropping idle HTTP/2 connections and tearing streams.
jon: do we see GOAWAY frames? That would be the LB or proxy asking to drain connections.
maya: some traces show GOAWAY from the edge with code=NO_ERROR followed by RST_STREAMs for active streams. Others show no GOAWAY, just abrupt RST_STREAM/CANCEL.
olivia: infra-oncall — did we roll anything overnight on the ALB/nginx fleet?
infra-oncall: no full fleet roll, but there was a partial router config push to adjust buffer sizes for large responses in eu-west. Rollout finished ~06:50. We reverted parts at 08:00 after CS flagged incidents.
carlos: buffering change could interact with HTTP/2 flow control. If the proxy buffers large server responses and stalls on window updates, it might block other streams and trigger resets. Also saw conntrack saturation on previous infra incidents — ephemeral port exhaustion can cause new connections to get NAT'ed weirdly.
jon: can we correlate with conntrack counters?
maya: checked node-exporter: conntrack_used jumped from 40k to 95k around 07:10 on a subset of edge nodes. conntrack_max is 100k. That coincides with the spike.
olivia: that sounds like NAT port exhaustion for egress. Some pods open lots of outbound TCP flows to other infra services (metrics, tracing). If ephemeral ports run out, the kernel can start dropping or reusing tuples. For long-lived HTTP/2 connections, that could manifest as weird resets.
jon: Proposed triage steps: 1) capture tcpdump on an affected edge node for a short window; 2) enable debug HTTP/2 logs on nginx for that node; 3) check ALB access logs for idle timeouts and connection termination codes.
maya: I ran a quick tcpdump on one node and saw a pattern: multiple FIN/ACKs from ALB to edge without preceding GOAWAY. Also saw KEEPALIVE probes (TCP) from client side, but the ALB closed first. Paste of pcap summary: 
```
07:13:57.102 IP alb-1.100.200.3.443 > edge-7.10.0.12.51812: Flags [R], seq 0, ack 0, win 0
07:13:57.103 IP edge-7.10.0.12.51812 > pod-10.1.2.34.443: Flags [F.], seq 2345, ack 9876, win 512
```
jon: ALB doing R? ALB sometimes resets TCP if target is unhealthy or timed out. Check target group deregistration events.
infra-oncall: looked at target group health history: several transient targets in eu-west had UNHEALTHY for ~90s around 07:11, then recovered. Health checks were 10s interval, 2 unhealthy threshold. No config change there.
carlos: health flapping + conntrack exhaustion suggests simultaneous resource pressure. Could be kernel hitting netfilter conntrack helper entries (related to HTTP/2 multiplexing?). Also check backlog and accept queue drops on the edge.
maya: metrics show listen_drops increasing on a few nodes. accept queue saturating. We also had a soft OOM on one nginx worker earlier.
jon: Action items: - add an A record (temporarily) to route a small % of traffic to a bypass NLB (no ALB) to see if ALB is the culprit - increase conntrack_max for the cluster nodes as quick mitigation - revert the buffer-size change we rolled - add tracing to capture HTTP/2 SETTINGS and window_update frames for deeper analysis
olivia: agree. For mitigation right now I can bump conntrack_max and ephemeral port range on eu-west node pool (if ops approves). Also will schedule a canary that skips the proxy chain to isolate ALB/NGINX.
infra-oncall: ops approved conntrack bump to 262144 and net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range expanded. Rolling patches to nodes now; expect pods to reconnect but should be fine with graceful restart.
carlos: after bump, monitor for a few minutes. If resets stop, it's likely conntrack. If still happening, we need to inspect ALB TCP termination behavior and nginx http2 buffer interactions.
maya: I reverted the buffer-size config and restarted a small subset of routers at 07:58. After conntrack bump and revert, stream resets dropped to baseline by ~08:05 in telemetry.
jon: still need root cause: why did conntrack jump? Were there increased ephemeral outbound connections?
maya: digging into egress metrics — a spike in control-plane telemetry fans out happened at 07:09 from a new rollout job. That job opened parallel HTTP connections to many internal endpoints for health/reporting. It was later throttled but created a short-lived burst.
olivia: we should add rate-limiting for that rollout job and prefer connection pooling over N requests in parallel. Also add an alert for conntrack usage nearing 80%.
carlos: long-term fix: move to keepalive across reverse-proxy chain, ensure ALB idle timeout >= nginx upstream timeout for HTTP/2, add instrumentation to log HTTP/2 GOAWAY and window updates, and tune buffering to not block streams. Consider moving to NLB with TLS passthrough for critical low-latency streams.
maya: opened an RFC with proposed changes and rollback plan. I also attached a small repro script to simulate long-lived streams + bursty egress to test conntrack behavior.
jon: nice. One note: when you run repro, include tcpdump and HTTP/2 frame logs. For nginx add: 
```
error_log /var/log/nginx/error.log debug;
# capture http2 frames with: nginx -V and enable stream_mod or use h2dump on the wire
```
infra-oncall: deploy-bot flagged: deploy 2026.03.18.edge-buffers revert completed at 07:58 UTC :white_check_mark:
deploy-bot: deploy 2026.03.18.edge-conntrack-bump started at 08:00 UTC
maya: thanks everyone. Will follow up in the RFC thread with lessons learned and a simple runbook for on-call (conntrack bump, check ALB health, revert buffer changes, canary bypass).
olivia: added a PagerDuty runbook entry to update conntrack thresholds and to check ALB target flapping next time.
carlos: closing loop: also add a Grafana panel for http2.streams.active and nginx listen_drops so this doesn't surprise us.
maya: closing here — resolved for now, will keep monitoring. :thumbsup:
